newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso closes strong amidst inflows.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso closes strong amidst inflows.

text.p: * Trades stay within Central Bank's desired range
The Philippine peso was boosted on Tuesday by the inflow of foreign portfolio money to close at its day-high of 26.306 from 26.327, traders said.
The day's average was at 26.315 versus the previous day's average of 26.328. Volume fell to $190.50 million from $212.50 million.
"There were sudden inflows from foreign investors," a dealer from a big bank said.
A trader said banks decided to sell their dollars after the Central Bank maintained its overnight rates, discouraging speculation in foreign exchange.

Usually, the Central Bank adjusts its overnight rates on a Tuesday to trend it with the movement in Treasury bill rates the previous day. The benchmark 91-day T-bill rate fell on Monday to 10.746 from 11.172 percent.
"After what happened last week, the Central Bank decided to keep the market calm by not cutting its overnight rates," another trader said.
